summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.17/867)

data.turoyo: Maḥtiwonne gozləkat (ḥazoye) d ǧam ʕal ʕaynayye mbahdəliwo ruḥayye. Saymiwo ruḥayye Šammo. Xəd uʕdo d koṯən harke, b riše di šato harke, mən kowe, mən kəmmile?
data.translation: They would put glass spectacles over their eyes and make themselves ridiculous. They would make themselves into Šammo. Like the one who comes here now, at New Year here, what is he, what do they call him?

rationale: First active Infectum-wa; overt ruḥayye reflexive keeps this separate from Detransitive morphology. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; interpretation rests on the Turoyo.

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: I naqqa u ʕAbdo (gaḥxo) d azze, maqlabbe bi saqiye dam maye w di čačma čik w mbahdəl... w mbahdəl hawi qašmar bayn daḥ ḥawrone (gaḥxo). Ha hano u ʕAbdano d be Yarəm-bučəq. Kəlle uʕdo harke. Kəlle harke yo.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: The time when Abdo (laughter) went, it tipped him into the water channel, and he got stuck at the fountain, and was made a fool of ... and was made a fool of, became a laughingstock among those friends. (Laughter.) There is this Abdo of the Yarəm-bučəq family. He is still here. Here he is.

rationale: Fills Detransitive Preterit with a physical mishap and explicit becoming a laughingstock; distinct from destitution and with preserved repetition. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; interpretation rests on the Turoyo.

data.translation: That Kurd came, insulted, greatly reviled the people, saying, 'How can you tie things on this tree like that! It is nothing! It is superstition!' He had stopped us all.

rationale: Fills active Preterit after three baseline examples: insulting a zero-marked human group in direct speech. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; interpretation rests on the Turoyo.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
before: in Schimpf und Schande kommen, beschämt dastehen;
after: in Schimpf und Schande kommen, beschämt dastehen; in einen erbärmlichen Zustand geraten;
rationale: The inherited 73/164 already describes torn clothes and misery, and 93/64 describes bereavement and destitution without a public shamer; make that existing broader result state explicit.

summary: The inherited glossary files the Arabic quadriliteral as stem I; do not create Q from a generic quadriliteral analysis.
Active ruḥi constructions deliberately represent self-disgracing action, contrasting with Detransitive disgrace or misery without an expressed external agent.
Detransitive Preterit includes resultant miserable condition, already visible at 73/164; 93/64 broadens its evidence from torn clothes to bereavement and starvation.
Actor and patient endings are distinct: mbahdeluxlan indexes a second-person actor and first-person plural affected group, whereas Infectum can use an independent pronoun (ono) or a suffix.
MAC kəmbahdela has an abstract religious topic; feminine object resumption may track ṭayuṯo rather than masculine mede. No religious technical sense follows from that participant choice.
Repeated free combinations with ruḥo or abstract objects do not establish an additional fixed idiom; all are kept within existing senses.
Keep the glossary stem I for this quadriliteral, as round one explicitly established. No Q stem is created.

Active Infectum-wa with ruḥayye expresses deliberate self-ridicule, while agentless mbahdəl/mbahdəli gives a resulting condition. Indefinite active agent in gəd mbahdelan is not a Detransitive just because English could be passive.
Social disgrace, verbal reviling and miserable state all fit the active and Detransitive meanings already retained or widened in round one. No new idiom or sense is needed.
The active Infectum cell already has six examples after round one; omit the lengthy telegram scene as a redundant routine example.
Does final -a in MAC Besim /10 resume feminine ṭayuṯo through kul mede, or have another analysis?
In 95/38 does ʕam ruḥux mean yourself too, or accompaniment with the preceding name object?
At 113/194 does plural -lan refer to the speaker's group or a pragmatic self-reference? The German has mich; the edition wording is retained.
Confirm the segmental contraction in 1sg mbahdanno and the scope of the result-state Detransitive in 93/64.
Confirm exact agent/object segmentation of gəd mbahdelan (1.21/1066); the source and context favour active indefinite agents with an affected first-person group.
Does bare mbahdəl at 1.17/857 distinguish eventive becoming disgraced from the resulting condition? Both fit the existing Detransitive sense.
Old age, a father's name and religion can stand as abstract patients of disgrace; these participant changes retain the same shaming meaning.
Wretched children directly confirm the round-one Detransitive gloss extension to a miserable condition; no new numbered sense.
